title.en: Games: a matrix and a tree (predicted 6)
title.zh: 博弈：一张矩阵和一棵树（预测题 6）

description.en: Dominant strategies and Nash equilibrium in a payoff matrix, why rivals end up in a prisoners’ dilemma, how repetition can rescue cooperation, and how to solve a game in turns by working backwards, with credible threats and commitment.
description.zh: 收益矩阵里的占优策略和纳什均衡，对手为什么会陷入囚徒困境，重复博弈怎样挽救合作，以及怎样倒推求解轮流行动的博弈，包括可信的威胁和承诺。

description.en: Believing any announced threat changes what a rival does
description.zh: 以为任何宣布的威胁都会改变对手的行为

title.en: Predicted question 6, as it could be printed

paras.en: (a) Two supermarkets, A and B, each choose a weekend price, High or Low. Weekly profits in \$000 (A, B): both High (50, 50); A High and B Low (10, 70); A Low and B High (70, 10); both Low (30, 30).
paras.zh: (a) 两家超市 A 和 B，各自选择周末价格：高价或低价。每周利润（千元，A 在前、B 在后）：都高价 (50, 50)；A 高 B 低 (10, 70)；A 低 B 高 (70, 10)；都低价 (30, 30)。

paras.en: **i.** Does either supermarket have a dominant strategy? (2 marks) **ii.** Find all Nash equilibria. (2 marks) **iii.** Explain why this is a prisoners' dilemma, and how playing the game every week could change the outcome. (4 marks)
paras.zh: **i.** 哪家超市有占优策略吗？（2 分）**ii.** 求所有纳什均衡。（2 分）**iii.** 解释为什么这是囚徒困境，以及每周都重复这个博弈会怎样改变结果。（4 分）

paras.en: (b) An entrant decides whether to enter a market held by an incumbent. If it stays out, the payoffs (entrant, incumbent) are (0, 100). If it enters, the incumbent either fights with a price war, (−10, 20), or accommodates, (30, 50).
paras.zh: (b) 一个潜在进入者决定是否进入一家在位厂商占据的市场。如果它不进入，收益（进入者，在位者）为 (0, 100)。如果进入，在位者要么打价格战 (−10, 20)，要么接纳 (30, 50)。

paras.en: **i.** Draw the game tree and find the subgame perfect equilibrium. (3 marks) **ii.** The incumbent announces that it will fight any entrant. Is the threat credible? (2 marks) **iii.** Before the entrant decides, the incumbent can spend 40 on extra capacity. Its payoffs net of the 40 then become 60 if the entrant stays out, 45 if it fights and 10 if it accommodates. Should it invest? (3 marks)
paras.zh: **i.** 画出博弈树并求子博弈完美均衡。（3 分）**ii.** 在位者宣布会对任何进入者开打。这个威胁可信吗？（2 分）**iii.** 在进入者决定之前，在位者可以花 40 扩充产能。扣除这 40 后，它的收益变为：进入者不进入时 60，开打时 45，接纳时 10。它应该投资吗？（3 分）

title.en: Why this is a likely question
title.zh: 为什么这道题很可能考

body.en: Game theory is taught with oligopoly, and the learning outcomes ask you to analyse strategic situations with it. The mock used it only inside Cournot.
body.zh: 博弈论和寡头一起讲，学习目标要求用它分析策略情境。模考只在古诺题里用到了它。

items.en: **A game**: players, the strategies each can choose, and a payoff for every combination. In (a) both choose at once without seeing the other; a **payoff matrix** lists all four combinations.
items.zh: **博弈**：参与者，每人能选的策略，以及每种组合下的收益。(a) 里两家同时选、看不到对方；**收益矩阵**列出全部四种组合。

items.en: In (b) the players move **in turn** and the second sees what the first did; a **game tree** shows the order.
items.zh: (b) 里参与者**轮流**行动，后动的人看得到先动的人做了什么；**博弈树**画出先后顺序。

items.en: **Dominant strategy, Nash equilibrium, subgame perfect, credible**: each is defined below where it is used.
items.zh: **占优策略、纳什均衡、子博弈完美、可信**：都在下面用到的地方定义。

title.en: A payoff matrix: best replies and Nash equilibrium
title.zh: 收益矩阵：最优反应和纳什均衡

paras.en: Does either supermarket have a dominant strategy? Find all Nash equilibria.
paras.zh: 哪家超市有占优策略吗？求所有纳什均衡。

text.en: Think as supermarket A. *If B charges High*: High earns A 50, Low earns 70; Low is better. *If B charges Low*: High earns 10, Low earns 30; Low is better again. Whatever B does, Low is better for A. A strategy that is best whatever the rival does is a **dominant strategy**. B's payoffs are the mirror image, so Low is dominant for B too.
text.zh: 站在超市 A 的角度想。*如果 B 定高价*：A 定高价赚 50，定低价赚 70；低价更好。*如果 B 定低价*：A 高价赚 10，低价赚 30；还是低价更好。不管 B 怎么做，低价对 A 都更好。不管对手怎么做都是最好的策略，叫**占优策略**（dominant strategy）。B 的收益是镜像，所以低价对 B 也是占优的。

text.en: A **Nash equilibrium** is a combination in which each player's choice is the best reply to the other's: nobody wants to change on their own. A quick method: for each column, mark A's best payoff; for each row, mark B's best payoff. A cell with both marked is a Nash equilibrium. Here only (Low, Low) is marked twice. (When both players have dominant strategies, the equilibrium is always where they meet.)
text.zh: **纳什均衡**是这样一种组合：每个人的选择都是对对方选择的最优反应，没人想单方面改变。一个快速方法：在每一列里标出 A 最好的收益；在每一行里标出 B 最好的收益。两个都被标出的格子就是纳什均衡。这里只有（低，低）被标了两次。（双方都有占优策略时，均衡总在两者交汇处。）

prompt.en: Is (High, High), where both earn 50, a Nash equilibrium?
prompt.zh: （高，高）两家各赚 50，是纳什均衡吗？

label.en: Yes: it gives both the most
label.zh: 是：它让双方都赚得最多

feedback.en: Best for both together is not the test; each player's own best reply is.
feedback.zh: 判断标准不是双方合起来最好，而是每个人自己的最优反应。

label.en: No: each could earn 70 by switching to Low while the other stays High
label.zh: 不是：对方保持高价时，每家改成低价都能赚 70

feedback.en: (Low, Low) is symmetric too; symmetry decides nothing.
feedback.zh: （低，低）也是对称的；对称不说明什么。

explain.en: From (High, High) each player gains 20 by deviating alone, so it is not an equilibrium.
explain.zh: 从（高，高）出发，任何一方单独偏离都能多赚 20，所以它不是均衡。

title.en: The prisoners’ dilemma, and what repetition changes
title.zh: 囚徒困境，以及重复博弈改变了什么

paras.en: Explain why this is a prisoners' dilemma, and how playing the game every week could change the outcome.
paras.zh: 解释为什么这是囚徒困境，以及每周都重复这个博弈会怎样改变结果。

text.en: Both supermarkets end up at (Low, Low) earning 30 each, although (High, High) would give each 50. Each one, acting in its own interest, makes both worse off. That is the **prisoners' dilemma**: individually rational choices produce an outcome that is worse for everyone. The cartel of predicted question 5 is the same game: keep the agreement (High) or cheat (Low).
text.zh: 两家最后停在（低，低），各赚 30，尽管（高，高）能让每家赚 50。每家都按自身利益行事，结果让两家都更差。这就是**囚徒困境**：每个人理性的选择，带来对所有人都更差的结果。预测题 5 的卡特尔就是同一个博弈：守约（高价）还是背叛（低价）。

text.en: Played once, nothing can be done. Played **every week without a known end**, the future becomes a weapon. Suppose each plays: *charge High as long as the other has always charged High; if it ever charges Low, charge Low for ever after* (a **trigger strategy**). Cheating now gains $70 - 50 = 20$ this week, but loses $50 - 30 = 20$ in every week after. If the future matters enough, cooperating at (High, High) is worth more than cheating. With a weekly discount factor $\delta$ (how much next week's dollar is worth today), cooperation holds when $20 \leq \frac{20\delta}{1 - \delta}$, that is $\delta \geq \frac12$.
text.zh: 只玩一次，没有办法。**每周都玩、且不知道何时结束**，未来就变成了武器。假设双方都采用：*只要对方一直定高价，我就定高价；对方只要有一次定低价，我就永远定低价*（**触发策略**，trigger strategy）。现在背叛，这周多赚 $70 - 50 = 20$，但之后每周都少赚 $50 - 30 = 20$。只要未来足够重要，在（高，高）合作就比背叛更值。设每周的贴现因子为 $\delta$（下周的一块钱今天值多少），合作成立的条件是 $20 \leq \frac{20\delta}{1 - \delta}$，即 $\delta \geq \frac12$。

title.en: If the last week is known
title.zh: 如果知道哪一周是最后一周

body.en: Then in the last week there is no future to protect, so both charge Low; knowing that, both charge Low the week before, and so on back to the first week. Cooperation needs an uncertain end.
body.zh: 那么最后一周没有未来要保护，双方都定低价；知道这一点，倒数第二周也都定低价，一直倒推到第一周。合作需要结束时间不确定。

say.en: Write H for High and L for Low, A's choice first. If B charges High, A earns more with Low:
say.zh: 用 H 表示高价、L 表示低价，A 的选择写在前面。B 定高价时，A 选低价赚得更多：

say.en: If B charges Low, Low is better for A again. So Low is A's dominant strategy, and by symmetry B's.
say.zh: B 定低价时，低价对 A 还是更好。所以低价是 A 的占优策略，由对称性也是 B 的。

say.en: The only cell where both play a best reply: the Nash equilibrium.
say.zh: 唯一一个双方都在做最优反应的格子：纳什均衡。

say.en: Both would be better off here: a prisoners' dilemma.
say.zh: 双方在这里都会更好：囚徒困境。

say.en: Repeated with a trigger strategy: this week's gain from cheating against the loss in every later week.
say.zh: 用触发策略重复博弈：本周背叛的收益，对比之后每周的损失。

outro.en: **Answer:** Low is a dominant strategy for both; the only Nash equilibrium is (Low, Low) with (30, 30), though (High, High) would give (50, 50): a prisoners' dilemma. Repeated indefinitely, trigger strategies can sustain (High, High) if the firms value the future enough ($\delta \geq \frac12$).
outro.zh: **答案：** 低价是双方的占优策略；唯一的纳什均衡是（低，低），收益 (30, 30)，尽管（高，高）能给 (50, 50)：囚徒困境。无限重复时，只要厂商足够看重未来（$\delta \geq \frac12$），触发策略可以维持（高，高）。

title.en: A game in turns: work backwards
title.zh: 轮流行动的博弈：倒着推

paras.en: Draw the game tree and find the subgame perfect equilibrium. The incumbent announces that it will fight any entrant. Is the threat credible?
paras.zh: 画出博弈树并求子博弈完美均衡。在位者宣布会对任何进入者开打。这个威胁可信吗？

blocks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 640 330" font-family="sans-serif"><rect width="640" height="330" fill="#ffffff"/><line x1="200" y1="60" x2="90" y2="180" stroke="#1f2328" stroke-width="2"/><text x="133.0" y="120.0" font-size="15" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="end">stay out</text><line x1="200" y1="60" x2="330" y2="180" stroke="#1f2328" stroke-width="4"/><text x="277.0" y="120.0" font-size="15" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="start">enter</text><line x1="330" y1="180" x2="230" y2="290" stroke="#c2410c" stroke-width="2"/><text x="268.0" y="235.0" font-size="15" fill="#c2410c" text-anchor="end">fight</text><line x1="330" y1="180" x2="450" y2="290" stroke="#c2410c" stroke-width="4"/><text x="402.0" y="235.0" font-size="15" fill="#c2410c" text-anchor="start">accommodate</text><circle cx="200" cy="60" r="7" fill="#1f2328"/><text x="200" y="44" font-size="16" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="middle">Entrant</text><circle cx="330" cy="180" r="7" fill="#c2410c"/><text x="346" y="185" font-size="16" fill="#c2410c" text-anchor="start">Incumbent</text><circle cx="90" cy="180" r="5" fill="#6b7077"/><circle cx="230" cy="290" r="5" fill="#6b7077"/><circle cx="450" cy="290" r="5" fill="#6b7077"/><text x="90" y="206" font-size="16" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="middle">(0, 100)</text><text x="230" y="316" font-size="16" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="middle">(-10, 20)</text><text x="450" y="316" font-size="16" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="middle">(30, 50)</text><text x="620" y="40" font-size="14" fill="#6b7077" text-anchor="end">(entrant, incumbent)</text></svg>

alt.en: Game tree: the entrant chooses stay out (0, 100) or enter; after entry the incumbent chooses fight (−10, 20) or accommodate (30, 50). Bold: accommodate, and so enter.
alt.zh: 博弈树：进入者选不进入 (0, 100) 或进入；进入后在位者选开打 (−10, 20) 或接纳 (30, 50)。粗线：接纳，因此进入。

caption.en: Read it from the bottom. The bold lines are the choices each player actually makes.
caption.zh: 从下往上读。粗线是每个参与者实际会做的选择。

text.en: When players move in turn, solve from the **last** move back to the first: **backward induction**. The last mover is the incumbent, after entry. Fighting gives it 20, accommodating 50: it accommodates. Now the entrant, who can foresee that: entering gives 30 (because the incumbent will accommodate), staying out 0. It enters. The equilibrium found this way, (Enter, Accommodate), is **subgame perfect**: every player's choice is a best reply at every point of the game, even at points not reached.
text.zh: 参与者轮流行动时，从**最后**一步往前倒着解：**逆向归纳**（backward induction）。最后行动的是进入发生后的在位者。开打得 20，接纳得 50：它会接纳。再看进入者，它能预见到这一点：进入得 30（因为在位者会接纳），不进入得 0。它会进入。这样求出的均衡（进入，接纳）是**子博弈完美**的：在博弈的每一个节点，每个人的选择都是最优反应，连没有走到的节点也是。

text.en: The threat to fight is **not credible**: once the entrant is in, fighting would cost the incumbent $50 - 20 = 30$, so it would not carry it out. A rational entrant ignores it. (There is another Nash equilibrium, (Stay out, Fight): if the entrant believed the threat, staying out would be its best reply. But it rests on a threat that would never be carried out; subgame perfection rules it out.)
text.zh: 开打的威胁**不可信**：一旦对方已经进来，开打会让在位者少赚 $50 - 20 = 30$，所以它不会真的这样做。理性的进入者会无视这个威胁。（还有另一个纳什均衡（不进入，开打）：如果进入者相信威胁，不进入就是它的最优反应。但这个均衡依赖一个永远不会兑现的威胁；子博弈完美把它排除了。）

title.en: Commitment: changing your own payoffs on purpose
title.zh: 承诺：故意改变自己的收益

paras.en: Before the entrant decides, the incumbent can spend 40 on extra capacity. Its payoffs net of the 40 then become 60 if the entrant stays out, 45 if it fights and 10 if it accommodates. Should it invest?
paras.zh: 在进入者决定之前，在位者可以花 40 扩充产能。扣除这 40 后，它的收益变为：进入者不进入时 60，开打时 45，接纳时 10。它应该投资吗？

text.en: Extra capacity is idle unless the incumbent produces a lot, so after investing, flooding the market (fighting) becomes its best reply: 45 against 10. The threat is now credible, because it is in the incumbent's own interest. The entrant foresees a fight and its −10, and stays out. The incumbent gets 60, more than the 50 it gets without investing. So it should invest: **commitment** works by giving up options, making the threat the incumbent's best choice.
text.zh: 多出来的产能只有大量生产才不会闲置，所以投资之后，充斥市场（开打）成了它的最优反应：45 对 10。威胁现在可信了，因为执行它符合在位者自己的利益。进入者预见到会开打、自己得 −10，于是不进入。在位者得 60，比不投资时的 50 多。所以应该投资：**承诺**靠放弃选择发挥作用，让威胁变成在位者自己的最佳选择。

blocks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 640 330" font-family="sans-serif"><rect width="640" height="330" fill="#ffffff"/><line x1="200" y1="60" x2="90" y2="180" stroke="#1f2328" stroke-width="4"/><text x="133.0" y="120.0" font-size="15" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="end">stay out</text><line x1="200" y1="60" x2="330" y2="180" stroke="#1f2328" stroke-width="2"/><text x="277.0" y="120.0" font-size="15" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="start">enter</text><line x1="330" y1="180" x2="230" y2="290" stroke="#c2410c" stroke-width="4"/><text x="268.0" y="235.0" font-size="15" fill="#c2410c" text-anchor="end">fight</text><line x1="330" y1="180" x2="450" y2="290" stroke="#c2410c" stroke-width="2"/><text x="402.0" y="235.0" font-size="15" fill="#c2410c" text-anchor="start">accommodate</text><circle cx="200" cy="60" r="7" fill="#1f2328"/><text x="200" y="44" font-size="16" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="middle">Entrant</text><circle cx="330" cy="180" r="7" fill="#c2410c"/><text x="346" y="185" font-size="16" fill="#c2410c" text-anchor="start">Incumbent</text><circle cx="90" cy="180" r="5" fill="#6b7077"/><circle cx="230" cy="290" r="5" fill="#6b7077"/><circle cx="450" cy="290" r="5" fill="#6b7077"/><text x="90" y="206" font-size="16" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="middle">(0, 60)</text><text x="230" y="316" font-size="16" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="middle">(-10, 45)</text><text x="450" y="316" font-size="16" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="middle">(30, 10)</text><text x="620" y="40" font-size="14" fill="#6b7077" text-anchor="end">(entrant, incumbent)</text><text x="620" y="62" font-size="14" fill="#c2410c" text-anchor="end">after spending 40 on capacity</text></svg>

alt.en: After spending 40 on capacity: stay out (0, 60); enter then fight (−10, 45) or accommodate (30, 10). The incumbent now fights, so the entrant stays out.
alt.zh: 花 40 扩充产能后：不进入 (0, 60)；进入后开打 (−10, 45) 或接纳 (30, 10)。在位者现在会开打，所以进入者不进入。

caption.en: The same tree with the incumbent's new payoffs. Backward induction now gives (Stay out, Fight).
caption.zh: 同一棵树换上在位者的新收益。逆向归纳现在给出（不进入，开打）。

prompt.en: Why does the incumbent's announcement fail but the capacity work?
prompt.zh: 为什么在位者的宣布没用，而扩充产能有用？

label.en: The capacity costs money, so the entrant is impressed
label.zh: 产能要花钱，所以进入者被震慑

feedback.en: Spending alone proves nothing; what matters is that fighting becomes the incumbent's best reply.
feedback.zh: 光花钱证明不了什么；关键是开打变成了在位者的最优反应。

label.en: The entrant cannot see the announcement
label.zh: 进入者看不到那个宣布

feedback.en: It sees it, and rightly ignores it.
feedback.zh: 它看得到，而且理所当然地无视了。

label.en: The capacity changes what is best for the incumbent after entry; words do not
label.zh: 产能改变了进入发生后对在位者最好的选择；话语不会

explain.en: A threat is credible only if carrying it out is the threatener's best move when the time comes.
explain.zh: 只有到时候执行威胁对威胁者自己是最好的，威胁才可信。

say.en: (i) The last move. Write $A$ for accommodate, $F$ for fight, $E$ for enter, $O$ for stay out. After entry the incumbent accommodates:
say.zh: (i) 最后一步。用 $A$ 表示接纳，$F$ 表示开打，$E$ 表示进入，$O$ 表示不进入。进入后在位者会接纳：

say.en: The entrant foresees accommodation, so it enters.
say.zh: 进入者预见到会被接纳，所以进入。

say.en: (ii) Carrying out the threat would cost the incumbent 30: not credible.
say.zh: (ii) 执行威胁会让在位者少赚 30：不可信。

say.en: (iii) With the capacity, fighting is the incumbent's best reply, so the entrant stays out.
say.zh: (iii) 有了产能，开打成了在位者的最优反应，所以进入者不进入。

say.en: The incumbent's payoff with the investment (already net of its cost) against without: invest.
say.zh: 在位者投资后的收益（已扣成本）对比不投资：应该投资。

outro.en: **Answer:** (i) (Enter, Accommodate), payoffs (30, 50). (ii) Not credible: once the entrant is in, fighting earns 20 against 50. (iii) Yes: the capacity makes fighting the incumbent's best reply (45 > 10), which deters entry and earns 60 > 50.
outro.zh: **答案：** (i)（进入，接纳），收益 (30, 50)。(ii) 不可信：对方进来后，开打得 20，接纳得 50。(iii) 应该：产能让开打成为在位者的最优反应（45 > 10），阻止了进入，得 60 > 50。

prompt.en: What does the entrant earn by entering, given that the incumbent accommodates?
prompt.zh: 在位者会接纳时，进入者进入能得多少？

paras.en: **a.i.** Yes, Low for both: if the rival is High, Low gives 70 > 50; if Low, 30 > 10. **ii.** The unique Nash equilibrium is (Low, Low), payoffs (30, 30). **iii.** Both would earn more at (High, High) (50 each), but each has an incentive to undercut: individually rational choices give a collectively worse outcome, a prisoners' dilemma. In an indefinitely repeated game, trigger strategies (charge High until the rival undercuts, then Low for ever) can sustain (High, High) if the future is valued enough, since a one-off gain of 20 is outweighed by losing 20 in every later week ($\delta \geq 1/2$).
paras.zh: **a.i.** 有，双方都是低价：对手高价时低价得 70 > 50；对手低价时得 30 > 10。**ii.** 唯一的纳什均衡是（低，低），收益 (30, 30)。**iii.** 双方在（高，高）都赚得更多（各 50），但都有压价的动机：个体理性的选择带来集体更差的结果，即囚徒困境。在无限重复博弈中，如果足够看重未来，触发策略（对手不压价就一直高价，一旦压价就永远低价）可以维持（高，高），因为一次性多赚的 20 抵不过之后每周少赚的 20（$\delta \geq 1/2$）。

paras.en: **b.i.** [Tree.] By backward induction the incumbent accommodates (50 > 20), so the entrant enters (30 > 0): SPE (Enter, Accommodate), (30, 50). **ii.** Not credible: after entry fighting gives the incumbent 20 < 50, so it would not carry out the threat. **iii.** With the capacity, fighting gives 45 > 10, so the threat becomes credible; the entrant stays out (0 > −10) and the incumbent earns 60 > 50. It should invest: a credible commitment deters entry.
paras.zh: **b.i.** [画树。] 逆向归纳：在位者接纳（50 > 20），所以进入者进入（30 > 0）：子博弈完美均衡（进入，接纳），(30, 50)。**ii.** 不可信：进入后开打只给在位者 20 < 50，它不会执行威胁。**iii.** 有了产能，开打得 45 > 10，威胁变得可信；进入者不进入（0 > −10），在位者得 60 > 50。应该投资：可信的承诺阻止了进入。

text.en: Where the marks are: in (a) the payoff comparisons that prove dominance, not just the answer; in (b) the tree with payoffs and the reasoning backwards from the last move; for credibility, the comparison *after* entry.
text.zh: 得分点：(a) 证明占优的收益比较，而不只是答案；(b) 带收益的博弈树，以及从最后一步倒推的推理；判断可信性要比较进入*之后*的收益。

title.en: Other games an exam can set
title.zh: 考试还可能出的其他博弈

items.en: **No dominant strategy, one equilibrium**: underline best replies anyway; an equilibrium can exist without dominant strategies.
items.zh: **没有占优策略、但有一个均衡**：照样标出最优反应；没有占优策略也可以有均衡。

items.en: **Two equilibria (coordination)**: two firms choosing a technical standard both prefer to match. (A, A) and (B, B) are both equilibria; history or a first mover decides which.
items.zh: **两个均衡（协调博弈）**：两家选技术标准，都希望和对方一致。（A，A）和（B，B）都是均衡；由历史或先行者决定是哪个。

items.en: **No equilibrium in pure strategies** (one wants to match, the other to differ): players randomise; this course rarely goes there.
items.zh: **没有纯策略均衡**（一方想一样、另一方想不一样）：参与者随机选择；这门课很少讲到这里。

items.en: **First-mover advantage in a tree**: the leader of predicted question 5 is a game tree with a continuous choice; backward induction is the same.
items.zh: **树里的先动优势**：预测题 5 的领导者就是一棵选择连续的博弈树；逆向归纳的做法一样。

items.en: Choosing the cell that is best for both as the Nash equilibrium.
items.zh: 把对双方都最好的格子当成纳什均衡。

items.en: In a tree, solving from the first move forward.
items.zh: 在树里从第一步往后解。

items.en: Counting the investment cost twice: the payoffs in (b iii) are already net of it.
items.zh: 把投资成本算两次：(b iii) 的收益已经扣除了它。

prompt.en: Two firms choose to advertise or not. Payoffs (firm 1, firm 2): both advertise (4, 4); 1 advertises, 2 does not (8, 2); 1 does not, 2 does (2, 8); neither (6, 6). What is the Nash equilibrium?
prompt.zh: 两家厂商选择做不做广告。收益（厂商 1，厂商 2）：都做 (4, 4)；1 做 2 不做 (8, 2)；1 不做 2 做 (2, 8)；都不做 (6, 6)。纳什均衡是什么？

feedback.en: Each would gain by advertising alone: 8 > 6.
feedback.zh: 任何一方单独做广告都能获益：8 > 6。

feedback.en: Advertising is dominant for both (8 > 6 and 4 > 2).
feedback.zh: 做广告对双方都是占优的（8 > 6，4 > 2）。

explain.en: Another prisoners' dilemma: both advertise and earn 4, though neither advertising would give 6.
explain.zh: 又一个囚徒困境：双方都做广告、各赚 4，尽管都不做能各赚 6。

prompt.en: After entry, fighting gives the incumbent 40 and accommodating 30. Is a threat to fight credible?
prompt.zh: 进入后，开打给在位者 40，接纳给 30。开打的威胁可信吗？

label.en: Yes: fighting is its best reply after entry
label.zh: 可信：进入后开打是它的最优反应
不可信：威胁从来都不可信

feedback.en: A threat is credible when carrying it out pays.
feedback.zh: 执行威胁划算时，威胁就可信。

label.en: Only if it announces it loudly

feedback.en: Announcing changes nothing; the payoffs decide.
feedback.zh: 宣布不改变任何东西；收益说了算。

explain.en: Work backwards: 40 > 30, so it would fight; the entrant, foreseeing that, stays out if fighting hurts it.
explain.zh: 倒着推：40 > 30，它会开打；进入者预见到这一点，如果开打对自己不利就不进入。
